Off-Grid Solar System for an RV

An off-grid RV solar system lets you power your refrigerator, lights, fans, laptops, TV, and other appliances without connecting to shore power or running a generator.

For most RVs, I recommend a 48V or 12V lithium battery system with 400–1,200W of solar panels, depending on your power consumption.

1. How an RV solar system works
Conceptual layout. A real installation also requires fuses, disconnects, appropriately sized wiring, grounding, and battery protection.

Off-Grid Solar System for an RV

An off-grid RV solar system lets you run lights, a refrigerator, fans, laptops, a water pump, and even an air conditioner without relying on campground hookups or a generator.

For most RVs, I recommend a 48V lithium battery system with 800–1,200W of solar panels if you plan to live off-grid regularly. For smaller camper vans or weekend trips, a 12V system is often more practical.
